messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: INC-2026-4523 triggered for api-hosted-us-east-1 - increased 5xx rates and P99 latency on Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Priority: P1

pagerduty: Incident assigned to oncall-ops (sophia)

sophia: I'm on it. Seeing elevated 502/504 from upstream auth proxy in us-east-1. Quick recap: Hosted API frontends returning 502s intermittently, Dedicated client pools seeing slow tail latency.

mike: Confirmed from synthetic checks and customer reports. UI shows spikes around 15:04 UTC.

derek: Any CloudWatch or ELB metrics we can jump into? I can start pulling ELB logs.

jess: copying logs now. Early chart: auth-proxy target group 5xx went from ~0.02% to 4.5% at 15:03 UTC.

sophia: Impact: all hosted endpoints in us-east-1, and Dedicated pools pinned to us-east-1. Some traffic routed to secondary region but not enough capacity for spike.

incident-bot: :information_source: Incident channel created: #inc-3092102468 (linked)

mike: Repro steps for infra: curl to api redwood-eu/prod returns 502 with body: 
```
{ "error": "upstream_auth_error", "code": 502 }
```

jess: ELB error codes are '504' from target group health checks and lots of 502s. Auth token validation latency spiking to 3s then timing out.

derek: I'm SSHing into the auth-proxy fleet in us-east-1 to check connection to identity provider. Starting tail on /var/log/proxy.log

oncall-ops: Allocated temporary routing policy: shift 20% of new traffic for Hosted to us-west-2 region, and scale dedicated pool burst capacity by 2 nodes (if available). Executing now.

sophia: Noting customer-facing: creating status page incident. Support, please hot-swap top affected customers. @jess open support ticket template and track impacted orgs.

jess: Created ticket RW-INC-3092102468 and added initial impact list (5 orgs with percent requests failing >10%). Links: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/RW-INC-3092102468

mike: Mitigation attempts: increasing auth-proxy replicas shows partial recovery in a subset of instances. Some proxies still failing with TLS handshake errors to auth provider.

derek: Observability note: our SaaS observability vendor (thirdparty-obs) is also reporting elevated ingest latency from us-east-1 which is delaying health ingestion. Correlating timestamps match.

sophia: So two dependent failures: identity provider rate limiting (502s) + observability ingestion lag. That explains slow detection and some flapping.

mike: Action list: 1) Contact identity provider support and request emergency quota bump 2) Ramp routing fallback to us-west-2 to protect customers 3) Engage vendor support for observability ingestion 4) Track Dedicated pool scale and preemptive handoffs.

jess: Reaching out to identity-provider-support@idp.example.com with logs and timestamps. Sent at 15:18 UTC.

derek: Quick mitigation script I ran to identify bad proxies and cordon them: 
```
for i in $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:service,Values=auth-proxy" ...); do
  latency=$(ssh $i 'tail -n 200 /var/log/proxy.log | grep latency | awk '{print $NF}' | tail -1)
  if [ $latency -gt 2000 ]; then
    aws elbv2 deregister-target --target-group-arn $TG --target-id $i
  fi
done
```

sophia: Good. We'll cordon the unhealthy proxies. Derek please coordinate with infra to avoid mass deregistration.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Temporary routing updated: 20% -> us-west-2 applied at 15:22 UTC

oncall-ops: Dedicated pool burst +2 requested; autoscaler reports success for 1 node, second node pending due to quota. Trying manual start.

mike: Observability vendor replied: "We're seeing a regional ingest backlog due to partial outage in us-east-1, working on backfill; we recommend delaying non-critical writes and using local metrics cache." They gave an incident ref OB-9932.

sophia: That's going to slow our analysis. We'll use ELB raw logs and app logs for now. Jess, please paste the customer impact template into the status page.

jess: Status page updated: "We are experiencing increased errors and latency in the US East (N. Virginia) region due to failures between our auth proxy and a third-party identity provider. Temporary routing and Dedicated pool scale-up in progress. We will provide updates every 15 minutes."

derek: Identity provider support responded: 'we're throttling requests from your tenant due to high burst; we can lift limits if you provide traffic patterns and request ramping.' Asking for emergency lift.

mike: In the meantime, can we enable token-cache fallback for Hosted API to reduce auth chattiness? There's a short config toggle.

sophia: Yes enable it for read-only endpoints and internal traffic. Jess, push config flag: 
```
service.auth.token_cache.enabled=true
service.auth.token_cache.ttl_ms=90000
```

jess: Flag toggled at 15:34 UTC. Rolling config to 60% of frontends to measure.

oncall-ops: Observed immediate drop in outgoing auth calls by ~40% on rolled frontends. Error rate decreased from 4.5% to ~1.6% for those instances.

sophia: Good. Now we need to stabilize Dedicated pools. Any customers still heavily impacted?

jess: Two customers still reporting >5% failures: org-phi, org-omega. Support contacted both with workarounds and advised to switch to secondary region endpoints.

derek: Identity provider just acknowledged emergency lift request; they will apply a 60s temporary quota increase while we implement backoff logic. ETA 10-15 minutes.

mike: Once quota is lifted, we should implement client-side exponential backoff + jitter to prevent recurrence. Add to postmortem action items.

sophia: I'll hand off to afternoon oncall (derek) in 25 minutes. Derek, please take lead for next hour and coordinate final rollback when healthy.

derek: Taking over. I'll keep this channel open and update every 10 minutes.

incident-bot: :star: Handoff recorded: sophia -> derek at 15:43 UTC

jess: Customer impact summary (initial): ~6 customers affected, 2 with significant errors. System level: Hosted API and Dedicated us-east-1 experienced increased 5xx and P99 latency; mitigations reduced impact by shifting traffic and token-cache fallback. Next update in 10 minutes.

sophia: Thanks team. Primary open items: confirm identity provider lift, finish Dedicated node add, full rollback of token-cache toggle once stable, follow-up postmortem and vendor RCA.

mike: Filing postmortem stub RW-POST-3092102468 and assigning action items.

oncall-ops: Marking incident as active. Will update when identity provider confirms lift.

incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Next scheduled update 15:53 UTC
